summary: A linguist, Carl Johan Sverdrup Marstrander studied at the University of Oslo (1903–1907) under Sophus Bugge and Alf Torp. He was Professor of Celtic and comparative linguistics at the School of Irish Learning (1909–1913) and at Oslo (1913–1953).

Carl Maria Franz Lorinser specialized in Indology and religious studies. He studied catholic theology at the University of Breslau (1839–1841), completed a Dr. Theol. at the University of Munich (~1840–1844), and also studied at Sapienza University of Rome (1842–1844).

Active in religious studies, Buddhist studies, and Indology, Carl Olson studied under mentor John Y. Fenton. He served as Teacher-Scholar Chair in the Humanities at Allegheny College, attested from 2005 to 2015.

Carl Paul Caspari worked in religious studies and linguistics. He studied at Leipzig under Heinrich Leberecht Fleischer (receiving his doctorate) and at Berlin. At the University of Oslo, he was appointed Lektor in 1847 and to a professorship in 1857.
Carl Rabe was an Indologist who completed his Ph.D. at the University of Breslau by 1845 under the doctoral supervision of Adolf Friedrich Stenzler.

Carl Salemann studied Iranian and Central Asian linguistics at Saint Petersburg State University (~1867–1875). He held posts at the university (~1876–1916), served as its librarian, became Adjunkt at the Russian Academy of Sciences (1886), and directed the Asiatic Museum (1890).

Carl Schuster worked in the fields of history, archaeology, and Sinology. He pursued his studies at Harvard University from around 1923 to 1930 and at the University of Vienna from around 1930 to 1934.

Carl Schütz was a scholar of Indology and linguistics. He studied at Halle-Wittenberg, under Franz Bopp (~1827–1830), and earned an honorary Ph.D. at Jena in 1831. He served as an Oberlehrer at Ratsgymnasium Bielefeld from 1834 to 1858.

Carl Shigeo Yamamoto specializes in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He completed his PhD at the University of Virginia under doctoral supervisors Jeffrey Hopkins and David Germano, also studying under Sonam Germano, William A. Magee, and Tsering Wangchuk.

A scholar of religion, Indology, and linguistics, Carl Siegfried studied at Halle-Wittenberg, Bonn, and under Albrecht Weber and Rudolf von Roth. He held posts at Trinity College Dublin and Schulpforta before serving as Old Testament professor at Jena (1875–1901).
Carl Suneson was an Indologist who studied at Stockholm University (1960–1966) under Siegfried Lienhard and V. Raghavan. In 1966, he became a Docent (Lecturer) at Stockholm University.

Carl Theodor Johannsen was an Indologist and linguist who studied at Kiel and Bonn. He taught oriental languages at Bonn (1830–1831) and Kiel (1831–1833) before becoming extraordinary professor in oriental philology and literature at the University of Copenhagen in 1833.

Carl W. Ernst specializes in Indology and religious studies. He studied at Stanford (A.B. 1968–1973) and Harvard (Ph.D. 1975–1981). He taught at Pomona College (1981–1992) and was Kenan Distinguished Professor at UNC Chapel Hill (1992–2022).

Carl Wilhelm Vollgraff studied classical linguistics and archaeology across Brussels, Utrecht, Göttingen, and Berlin under Leo and Wilamowitz-Moellendorff. He served as professor of Greek language and literature at the University of Groningen (1908–1916) and Utrecht University (1917–1946).

Carl William Belser worked in linguistics and Indology, earning degrees at Michigan and Leipzig under Friedrich Delitzsch. He taught at Mount Morris and Carthage, returned to Michigan in German, French, and Oriental Languages, and became Latin Department head at Colorado in 1893.

Historian and Indologist Carl von Noorden studied at Bonn, Marburg, Berlin, and Paris under Martin Haug and Leopold von Ranke. He was Professor of History at Greifswald (1868–1870), Marburg (1870–1873), Tübingen (1873–1876), Bonn (1876–1877), and Leipzig (1877).

Carl-Martin Edsman worked in religious studies. He studied at Uppsala University, Lund University, and the University of Paris (~1937–1938). He later held academic posts at Lund University (~1940–1950) and Uppsala University (~1950–1977).

Carlo Bernheimer was an Indologist who studied at the University of Bologna (~1897–1902) under Francesco Lorenzo Pullè. He served as Docent of Sanskrit at the University of Bologna from 1906 to 1938, and held a post there in 1945.

Carlo Della Casa, an Indologist, studied at the University of Turin from around 1947 to 1951 under Mario Vallauri. He later held an academic post at the University of Palermo from around 1969 to 1973.

Indologist Carlo Formichi studied in Naples under Kerbaker, Vienna under Bühler, and Kiel under Deussen and Oldenberg. He held teaching posts at Naples, Bologna, and Pisa, before serving as Professor of Sanskrit at Sapienza University of Rome (1914–1941).
